content: Elaine Gottschall (August 18, 1921 – September 5, 2005), who held a Bachelor of Arts and a Master of Science degree, was the author of the book Breaking the Vicious Cycle: Intestinal Health Through Diet. She developed and promoted the Specific Carbohydrate Diet (SCD), a dietary approach aimed at managing and treating intestinal bowel disorders. Her book provided guidance for individuals suffering from such conditions, offering an alternative method to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life. Numerous accounts exist of individuals who were on the verge of undergoing colectomy (surgical removal of the colon) but were able to avoid the procedure by adhering to this dietary regimen, ultimately achieving symptom control and regaining normal functionality. In her later years, Gottschall expanded her focus to explore the potential benefits of the Specific Carbohydrate Diet for children with developmental disorders, including autism. She dedicated significant time and effort to supporting parents, both through online forums and in-person interactions, offering guidance and encouragement. Her work was deeply influenced by the research of Dr. Sydney Haas, a physician she consulted while seeking treatment for her young daughter’s irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). By implementing Dr. Haas’s recommendations, Gottschall successfully managed her daughter’s condition, thereby avoiding the need for a distressing colectomy.
